nodes.statement: Let $m\geq 1$. If $f:G\to\bbr$ is such that $\bbe_x f(x)=0$ and $\abs{f(x)}\leq 2$ for all $x$ then \[\bbe_{x_1,\ldots,x_n} \abs{\sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i)}^{2m} \leq (4mn)^{m}.\]
nodes.name: Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequality
nodes.statement_short: Moment bound $(4mn)^m$ for sums of i.i.d. bounded mean-zero real samples.
assumptions: $f:G\to\bbr$ is such that $\bbe_x f(x)=0$ and $\abs{f(x)}\leq 2$ for all $x$
nodes.label: mzi

nodes.statement: Let $S$ be the left-hand side. Since $0=\bbe_y f(y)$ we have, by the triangle inequality, and H\"{o}lder's inequality, \begin{align} S & = \bbe_{x_1, \dots, x_n}\left\lvert \sum_i f(x_i) - \bbe_{y_i} f(y_i)\right\rvert^{2m} \\ & = \bbe_{x_1, \dots, x_n} \left\lvert\bbe_{y_i}\brac{\sum_i f(x_i) - f(y_i)}\right\rvert^{2m} \\ & \le \bbe_{x_1,\dots,y_n} \left\lvert \sum_i f(x_i) - f(y_i)\right\rvert^{2m} \end{align} Changing the role of $x_i$ and $y_i$ makes no difference here, but multiplies the $i$ summand by $\{-1,+1\}$, and therefore for any $\epsilon_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, \[ S \leq\bbe_{x_1,\ldots,y_n}\left\lvert \sum_i \epsilon_i(f(x_i)-f(y_i))\right\rvert^{2m}.\] In particular, if we sample $\epsilon_i\in\{-1,+1\}$ uniformly at random, then \[ S \leq\bbe_{\epsilon_i} \bbe_{x_1,\ldots,y_n}\left\lvert \sum_i \epsilon_i(f(x_i)-f(y_i))\right\rvert^{2m}.\] We now change the order of expectation and consider the expectation over just $\epsilon_i$, viewing the $f(x_i)-f(y_i)=z_i$, say, as fixed quantities. For any $z_i$ we can expand $\bbe_{\epsilon_i} \lvert \sum_i \epsilon_iz_i\rvert^{2m}$ and then bound it from above, using the triangle inequality and $\abs{z_i}\leq 4$, by \[4^{2m}\sum_{k_1+\cdots+k_n=2m}\binom{2m}{k_1,\ldots,k_n}\abs{\bbe\epsilon_1^{k_1}\cdots \epsilon_n^{k_n}}.\] The inner expectation vanishes unless each $k_i$ is even, when it is trivially one. Therefore the above quantity is exactly \[\sum_{l_1+\cdots+l_n=m}\binom{2m}{2l_1,\ldots,2l_n}\leq m^mn^m,\] since for any $l_1+\cdots+l_n=m$, \[\binom{2m}{2l_1,\ldots,2l_n}\leq m^m\binom{m}{l_1,\ldots,l_n}.\] This can be seen, for example, by writing both sides out using factorials, yielding \[\frac{(2m)!}{(2l_1)!\cdots (2l_n)!}\leq \frac{(2m)!}{2^mm!}\frac{m!}{l_1!\cdots l_n!}\leq m^m\frac{m!}{l_1!\cdots l_n!}.\]
nodes.name: Proof of Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequality
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrisation with random signs, then expand the $2m$-th moment and count even exponent patterns.

nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon\in (0,1]$ and $k\geq 1$. Let $K\geq 2$ and $A,S\subseteq G$ with $\lvert A+S\rvert\leq K\lvert A\rvert$. Let $B,C\subseteq G$. Let $\eta=\min(1,\lvert C\rvert/\lvert B\rvert)$. There exists $T\subseteq G$ such that \[\lvert T\rvert \geq K^{-4096\lceil \lo{\eta}\rceil k^2\epsilon^{-2}}\lvert S\rvert\] such that \[\| \mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C-\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C\|_{\infty}\leq \epsilon.\]

nodes.statement_short: The $k$-fold convolution of $\mu_T$ almost fixes $\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast\mu_C$ in $L^\infty$.
assumptions: Let $K\geq 2$ and $A,S\subseteq G$ with $\lvert A+S\rvert\leq K\lvert A\rvert$.

nodes.statement: Let $T$ be as in Theorem~\ref{linfty_ap} with $\epsilon$ replaced by $\epsilon/k$. Note that, for any $x\in G$, \[\mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C(x)=\frac{1}{\lvert T\rvert^k}\sum_{t_1,\ldots,t_k\in T}\tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_k}\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C(x).\] It therefore suffices (by the triangle inequality) to show, for any fixed $x\in G$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_k\in T$, that with $F=\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C$, we have \[\lvert \tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_k}F(x)-F(x)\rvert \leq \epsilon.\] This follows by the triangle inequality applied $k$ times if we knew that, for $1\leq l\leq k$, \[\lvert \tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_l}F(x)-\tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_{l-1}}F(x)\rvert \leq \epsilon/k.\] We can write the left-hand side as \[\lvert \tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_l}F(x)-\tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_{l-1}}F(x)\rvert=\lvert \tau_{t_l}F(x-t_1-\cdots-t-{l-1})-F(x-t_1-\cdots-t-{l-1})\rvert.\] The right-hand side is at most \[\| \tau_{t_l}F-F\|_\infty\] and we are done by choice of $T$.
nodes.name: Proof of Boosted $L_\infty$ almost periodicity
nodes.statement_short: Use the $L_\infty$ almost-periods with $\epsilon/k$ and telescope with the triangle inequality $k$ times.

nodes.statement: Using the convexity of $t\mapsto e^{tx}$ (for all $x\geq 0$ and $t\in[-1,1]$) we have \[e^{tx}\le \cosh(x)+t\sinh(x).\] It follows (taking $x=\lvert z\rvert$ and $t=\Re(z)/\lvert z\rvert$) that, for any $z\in \mathbb{C}$, \[e^{\Re z}\le \cosh \lvert z\rvert +\Re(z/\lvert z\rvert)\sinh \lvert z\rvert.\] In particular, if $c_\gamma\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\lvert c_\gamma\rvert=1$ is such that $\widehat{f}(\gamma)=c_\gamma\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert$, then \begin{align*} e^{\Re f(x)} &= \exp\left( \Re \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\widehat{f}(\gamma)\gamma(x)\right)\\ &=\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma} \exp\left( \Re \widehat{f}(\gamma)\gamma(x)\right)\\ &\le \prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma}\left( \cosh \lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert +\Re c_\gamma \gamma(x)\sinh \lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right). \end{align*} Therefore \[\E_x e^{\Re f(x)}\le \E_x \prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma} \left( \cosh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert+\Re c_\gamma \gamma(x)\sinh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right).\] Using $\Re z=(z+\overline{z})/2$ the product here can be expanded as the sum of \[\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2}\frac{c_\gamma}{2}\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_3}\frac{\overline{c_\gamma}}{2}\left(\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_1}\cosh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right)\left(\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2\cup\Gamma_3}\sinh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right)\left(\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2}\gamma-\sum_{\lambda\in \Gamma_3}\lambda\right)(x)\] as $\Gamma_1\sqcup \Gamma_2\sqcup \Gamma_3=\Gamma$ ranges over all partitions of $\Gamma$ into three disjoint parts. Using the definition of dissociativity we see that \[\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2}\gamma-\sum_{\lambda\in \Gamma_3}\lambda\neq 0\] unless $\Gamma_2=\Gamma_3=\emptyset$. In particular summing this term over all $x\in G$ gives $0$. Therefore the only term that survives averaging over $x$ is when $\Gamma_1=\Gamma$, and so \[\E_x e^{\Re f(x)}\le \prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma} \cosh \lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert.\] The conclusion now follows using $\cosh(x) \le e^{x^2/2}$ and $\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma}\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert^2=\| f\|_2^2$. The second conclusion follows by applying it to $f(x)$ and $-f(x)$ and using \[e^{\abs{y}}\le e^y+e^{-y}.\]
nodes.name: Proof of Rudin's exponential inequality
nodes.statement_short: Convexity bound $e^{tx}\le\cosh x+t\sinh x$, expand the product; dissociativity kills all cross terms on averaging.

nodes.statement:
Let $A'\subseteq A$ be a maximal dissociated subset (this exists and is non-empty, since trivially any singleton is dissociated). We have $\abs{A'}\le K$ by assumption. Let $S$ be the span on the right-hand side. It is obvious that $A'\subseteq S$. Suppose that $x\in A ackslash A'$. Then $A'\cup\{x\}$ is not dissociated by maximality. Therefore there exists some $y\in G$ and two distinct sets $B,C\subseteq A'\cup \{x\}$ such that \[\sum_{b\in B}b = y = \sum_{c\in C} c.\] If $x
ot\in B$ and $x
ot\in C$ then this contradicts the dissociativity of $A'$. If $x\in B$ and $x\in C$ then we have \[\sum_{b\in B ackslash x}b=y-x=\sum_{c\in C ackslash x}c,\] again contradicting the dissociativity of $A'$. Without loss of generality, therefore, $x\in B$ and $x
ot\in C$. Therefore \[x=\sum_{c\in C}c - \sum_{b\in B ackslash x}b\] which is in the span as required.
nodes.name: Proof of Span of sets without large dissociated subsets
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal dissociated subset; maximality expresses every other element as a signed sum.

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $f:G\to \bbc$. Let $\eta >0$ and $\alpha=N^{-1}\norm{f}_1^2/\norm{f}_2^2$. There exists some $\Delta\subseteq \Delta_\eta(f)$ such that \[\abs{\Delta}\le \lceil e\mathcal{L}(\alpha)\eta^{-2}\rceil \] and \[\Delta_\eta(f)\subseteq \left\{ \sum_{\gamma\in\Delta}c_\gamma \gamma : c_\gamma\in \{-1,0,1\} \right\}.\]
nodes.name: Chang's lemma
nodes.statement_short: The large spectrum lies in the $\{-1,0,1\}$-span of $O(\mathcal{L}(\alpha)\eta^{-2})$ characters.
assumptions: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $f:G\to \bbc$.
nodes.label: chang

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{diss_span} it suffices to show that $\Delta_\eta(f)$ contains no dissociated set with at least \[K= \lceil e\mathcal{L}(\alpha)\eta^{-2}\rceil+1\] many elements. Suppose not, and let $\Delta\subseteq \Delta_\eta(f)$ be a dissociated set of size $K$. Then by Lemma~\ref{diss_energy} we have, for any $m\geq 1$, \[E_{2m}(\Delta)\le m!K^m.\] On the other hand, by Lemma~\ref{spec_hoelder}, \[\eta^{2m}\alpha K^{2m}\le E_{2m}(\Delta).\] Rearranging these bounds, we have \[K^m \le m! \alpha^{-1}\eta^{-2m}\le m^m\alpha^{-1}\eta^{-2m}.\] Therefore $K\le \alpha^{-1/m}m\eta^{-2}$. This is a contradiction to the choice of $K$ if we choose $m=\mathcal{L}(\alpha)$, since $\alpha^{-1/m}\le e$.
nodes.name: Proof of Chang's lemma
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction: a large dissociated subset of the spectrum would violate the energy upper and lower bounds with $m=\mathcal{L}(\alpha)$.

nodes.statement: Let $p\geq 2$ be an even integer. Let $B_1,B_2\subseteq G$ and $\mu=\mu_{B_1}\circ\mu_{B_2}$. For any finite set $A\subseteq G$ and function $f:G\to\bbr_{\geq 0}$ there exist $A_1\subseteq B_1$ and $A_2\subseteq B_2$ such that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2}, f\rangle \norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p\leq 2\langle (\ind{A}\circ \ind{A})^p,f\rangle_\mu\] and \[\min\brac{\frac{\abs{A_1}}{\abs{B_1}},\frac{\abs{A_2}}{\abs{B_2}}}\geq \frac{1}{4}\abs{A}^{-2p}\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^{2p}.\]

nodes.statement_short: Dependent random choice: write the moment as a sum over $s\in G^p$ of $A_1(s),A_2(s)$ and discard small pairs. Cauchy-Schwarz with threshold $M$ shows the large pairs carry half the mass.

nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon,\delta >0$ and $p\geq \max(2,\epsilon^{-1}\log(2/\delta))$ be an even integer. Let $B_1,B_2\subseteq G$, and let $\mu=\mu_{B_1}\circ\mu_{B_2}$. For any finite set $A\subseteq G$, if \[S=\{ x\in G: \ind{A}\circ \ind{A}(x)>(1-\epsilon)\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}\},\] then there are $A_1\subseteq B_1$ and $A_2\subseteq B_2$ such that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ\mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle \geq 1-\delta\] and \[\min\brac{\frac{\abs{A_1}}{\abs{B_1}},\frac{\abs{A_2}}{\abs{B_2}}}\geq \frac{1}{4}\abs{A}^{-2p}\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^{2p}.\]

nodes.statement_short: Apply dependent random choice with $f=1_{G\setminus S}$ and bound the complement mass by $(1-\epsilon)^p$.

assumptions: $A_1,A_2,S\subseteq \bbf_q^n$ are such that $A_1$ and $A_2$ both have density at least $\alpha$

nodes.label: ap_in_ff

nodes.statement: (In this proof we write $G=\mathbb{F}_q^n$.) Let $k=\lceil \lo(\epsilon\alpha/4)\rceil$. Note that $\lvert A_1+G\rvert=\lvert G\rvert\leq \alpha^{-1}\lvert A\rvert$. Furthermore, $\lvert A_2\rvert/\lvert S\rvert\geq \alpha$. Therefore by Theorem~\ref{linfty_ap_boosted} there exists some $T\subseteq G$ with \[\lvert T\rvert \geq \exp(-2^{16}\lo(\alpha)^2k^2\epsilon^{-2})\lvert S\rvert\] such that \[\| \mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}-\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}\|_{\infty}\leq \epsilon/4.\] Let $\Delta=\Delta_{1/2}(\mu_T)$ and \[V = \{ x \in G : \gamma(x)=1\textrm{ for all }\gamma\in\Delta\}.\] Note that \[\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle = \langle \mu_V,\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}\rangle=\frac{1}{\abs{V}}\sum_{v\in V}\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)\] and \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle = \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ\ind{S}(0).\] Therefore \[\abs{\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle-\langle \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle}\leq \frac{1}{\abs{V}}\sum_{v\in V}\abs{\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)-\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(0)}.\] In particular it suffices to show that, for any $v\in V$, \[\abs{\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)-\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(0)}\leq \epsilon.\] By the triangle inequality and construction of $T$, it suffices to show that \[\abs{\mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)-\mu_T^{(k)}\ast\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(0)}\leq \epsilon/2.\] By the Fourier transform we have, for any $x\in G$, \[\mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma\in \widehat{G}}\widehat{\mu_T}(\gamma)^k\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)\gamma(x).\] Therefore the left-hand side of the desired inequality is, by the triangle inequality, at most \[\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma\in \widehat{G}}\abs{\widehat{\mu_T}(\gamma)}^k\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)}\abs{\gamma(v)-1}.\] By choice of $v\in V$ the summand vanishes when $\gamma\in\Delta$. When $\gamma\not\in \Delta$ the summand is bounded above by \[2^{1-k}\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)}.\] Therefore the left-hand side of the desired inequality is at most \[2^{1-k}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma}\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)}\leq 2^{1-k}\abs{S}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma}\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)}\] using the trivial bound $\lvert\widehat{\ind{S}}\rvert\leq \abs{S}$. By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality the sum on the right is at most \[\brac{\sum_\gamma \abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}}^2}^{1/2}\brac{\sum_\gamma \abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}}^2}^{1/2}.\] By Parseval's identity this is at most $\alpha^{-1}$. Therefore the desired inequality follows from \[2^{1-k}\abs{S}\frac{1}{N}\alpha^{-1}\leq 2^{1-k}\alpha^{-1}\leq \epsilon/2.\] It remains to check the codimension of $V$. For this, let $\Delta'\subseteq \Delta$ be as provided by Chang's lemma, Lemma~\ref{chang}, so that \[\Delta\subseteq \left\{ \sum_{\gamma\in\Delta'}c_\gamma \gamma : c_\gamma\in \{-1,0,1\} \right\}.\] Let \[W= \{ x \in G : \gamma(x)=1\textrm{ for all }\gamma\in\Delta'\}.\] It follows that $W\leq V$, so it suffices to bound the codimension of $W$. This we can bound trivially using the bound from Chang's lemma and the fact that $\lo(\delta)=\log(e^2/\delta)\leq 2+\log(1/\delta)\leq 4\log(1/\delta)$, provided $\log(1/\delta)\geq 1$, so \[\abs{\Delta'}\leq \lceil 4e\mathcal{L}(\delta)\rceil\leq 2^7\log(1/\delta),\] where \[\delta=\abs{T}/N\geq \exp(-2^{16}\lo(\alpha)^2k^2\epsilon^{-2}),\] so \[\mathrm{codim}(V)\leq \abs{\Delta'}\leq 2^{23}\lo(\alpha)^2k^2\epsilon^{-2}\leq 2^{25}\lo(\alpha)^2\lo(\epsilon \alpha/4)^2\epsilon^{-2},\] and now use $\lo(\epsilon\alpha/4)\leq 2\lo(\epsilon\alpha)$, say.

nodes.statement_short: Take boosted almost-periods $T$ and let $V$ annihilate the large spectrum of $\mu_T$; Fourier expansion bounds the error. Chang's lemma bounds the codimension of $V$.

nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon >0$ and $\mu\equiv 1/N$. If $A,C\subseteq G$, where $C$ has density at least $\gamma$, and \[\abs{N\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A,\mu_C\rangle -1}>\epsilon\] then, if $f=(\mu_A-1/N)$, $\norm{f\circ f}_{p(\mu)} \geq \epsilon /2N$ for $p=2\lceil \lo(\gamma)\rceil$.
nodes.name: Global dichotomy
nodes.statement_short: Deviation of $N\langle\mu_A\ast\mu_A,\mu_C\rangle$ from 1 forces a large $L^p$ norm of $f\circ f$.
assumptions: $A,C\subseteq G$, where $C$ has density at least $\gamma$
nodes.label: global_dichotomy

nodes.statement: By H\"{o}lder's inequality, for any $p\geq 1$ \[\epsilon < \abs{ N\langle \mu_A \ast \mu_A - 1/N, \mu_C \rangle } \leq \norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1/N}_p\gamma^{-1/p}N^{1-1/p}.\] In particular if we choose $p=2\lceil\lo(\gamma)\rceil$ then $\gamma^{-1/p}\leq e^{1/2}\leq 2$ and so we deduce that, by Lemma~\ref{ast_expand}, \[\norm{f\ast f}_{p}\geq \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon N^{1/p-1}.\] It remains to use Lemmas~\ref{ast_expand} and \ref{circ_expand} and apply Lemma~\ref{ast_le_circ}, and note that we can pass from the $L^p$ norm to the $L^p(\mu)$ norm losing a factor of $N^{1/p}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Global dichotomy
nodes.statement_short: Hölder's inequality with $p=2\lceil\mathcal{L}(\gamma)\rceil$, then the expansion identities and $\|f\ast f\|\le\|f\circ f\|$.

nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. If $A,C\subseteq \bbf_q^n$, where $C$ has density at least $\gamma$, and \[\abs{N\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A,\mu_C\rangle -1}> \epsilon\] then there is a subspace $V$ of codimension \[\leq 2^{171}\epsilon^{-24}\lo(\alpha)^4\lo(\gamma)^4.\] such that $\norm{\ind{A}\ast \mu_V}_\infty \geq (1+\epsilon/32)\alpha$.

nodes.statement_short: Large deviation of the 3AP-type count gives a density increment on a subspace of small codimension.

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~ef{global_dichotomy}, if $f=\mu_A-1/N$, \[
orm{f\circ f}_{p(\mu)}\geq \epsilon /2N,\] where $p=2\lceil \lo(\gamma)ceil\leq 4\lo(\gamma)$. By Lemma~ef{unbalancing} there exists some $p'$ such that \[p'\leq 128\epsilon^{-1}\log(96/\epsilon)\lo(\gamma)\] such that \[
orm{f\circ f+1/N}_{p'(\mu)}\geq (1+\epsilon/4)/N.\] By Lemma~ef{circ_expand} $f\circ f+1/N=\mu_A\circ \mu_A$. Let $q=2\lceil p'+2^8\epsilon^{-2}\log(64/\epsilon)ceil$. By Corollary~ef{sift_cor}, there are $A_1,A_2$, both of density $\geq \alpha^{2q}$ such that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}angle \geq 1-\epsilon/32\] where \[S=\{x : \mu_A\circ \mu_A(x)\geq (1-\epsilon/16)\| \mu_A\circ \mu_A\|_{q(\mu)}\}.\] Since \[\| \mu_A\circ \mu_A\|_{q(\mu)}\geq \| \mu_A\circ \mu_A\|_{p'(\mu)}\geq (1+\epsilon/4)/N\] we know \[S\subseteq S'=\{x : \mu_A\circ \mu_A(x)\geq (1+\epsilon/8)/N\}.\] By Theorem~ef{ap_in_ff} (applied with $\epsilon$ replaced by $\epsilon/32$) there is a subspace $V$ of codimension \[\leq 2^{37}\lo(\alpha^{2q})^2\lo(\epsilon\alpha^{2q}/32)^2\epsilon^{-2}\] such that \[\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S'}angle \geq 1-	frac{1}{16}\epsilon.\] Using $\lo(xy)\leq x^{-1}\lo(y)$ we have \[\lo(\epsilon \alpha^{2q}/32)\leq 32\epsilon^{-1}\lo(\alpha^{2q}),\] and we also use $\lo(x^y)\leq y\lo(x)$ to simplify the codimension bound to \[\leq 2^{51}q^4\lo(\alpha)^4\epsilon^{-4}.\] We further note that (using $\log x\leq x$ say) \[q\leq 2^{10}p'\epsilon^{-2}\log(64/\epsilon)\leq 2^{30}\epsilon^{-5}\lo(\gamma).\] Therefore the desired codimension bound follows. Finally, by definition of $S'$, it follows that  egin{align*} (1+\epsilon/32)/N &\leq ((1+\epsilon/8)/N)(1-\epsilon/16)\ &\leq \langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\mu_A\circ \mu_Aangle\ &\leq 
orm{\mu_V\ast \mu_A}_\infty 
orm{\mu_{A}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \mu_{A_1}}_1\ &= 
orm{\mu_V\ast \ind{A}}_\infty\abs{A}^{-1}, \end{align*} and the proof is complete.

nodes.statement_short: Global dichotomy, unbalancing, then sifting and finite-field almost periodicity give a density increment on a subspace.

nodes.statement: Let $t\geq 0$ be maximal such that there is a sequence of subspaces $\bbf_q^n=V_0\geq \cdots \geq V_t$ and associated $A_i\subseteq V_i$ with $A_0=A$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item for $0\leq i\leq t$ there exists $x_i$ such that $A_i\subseteq A-x_i$, \item with $\alpha_i=\abs{A_i}/\abs{V_i}$ we have \[\alpha_{i+1}\geq \frac{65}{64}\alpha_i\] for $0\leq i<t$, and \item \[\mathrm{codim} (V_{i+1}) \leq \mathrm{codim}(V_i)+O(\lo(\alpha)^8)\] for $0\leq i<t$. (here the second summand should be replaced with whatever explicit codimension bound we get from the above). \end{enumerate} Note this is well-defined since $t=0$ meets the requirements, and this process is finite and $t \ll \lo(\alpha)$, since $\alpha_i\leq 1$ for all $i$. Therefore \[\mathrm{codim}(V_t) \ll \lo(\alpha)^9.\] Suppose first that \[\lvert V_t\rvert\langle \mu_{A_t}\ast \mu_{A_t},\mu_{2\cdot A_t}\rangle<1/2.\] In this case we now apply Proposition~\ref{di_in_ff} to $A_t\subseteq V_t$ with $\epsilon=1/2$ (note that $N=\lvert V_t\rvert$ and all inner product, $\mu$ etc, are relative to the ambient group $V_t$ now). Therefore there is a subspace $V\leq V_t$ of codimension (relative to $V_t$) $\ll \lo(\alpha)^8$ such that there exists some $x\in V_t$ with \[\frac{\lvert (A_t-x)\cap V\rvert}{\lvert V\rvert}=1_{A_t}\ast \mu_V(x)=\| 1_{A_t}\ast \mu_V\|_\infty \geq (1+1/64)\alpha_t,\] which contradicts the maximality of $t$, letting $V_{t+1}=V$ and $A_{t+1}=(A_t-x)\cap V_t$. Therefore \[\lvert V_t\rvert\langle \mu_{A_t}\ast \mu_{A_t},\mu_{2\cdot A_t}\rangle\geq 1/2.\] By Lemma~\ref{no3aps_inner_prod} the left-hand side is equal to $\lvert V_t\rvert/\lvert A_t\rvert^2$, and therefore \[\alpha^2 \leq \alpha_t^2 \leq 2/\lvert V_t\rvert.\] By the codimension bound the right-hand side is at most \[2q^{O(\lo(\alpha)^9)-n}.\] If $\alpha^2 \leq 2q^{-n/2}$ we are done, otherwise we deduce that $\lo(\alpha)^9 \gg n$ as required.

nodes.name: Centre the sum and apply the triangle and Hölder inequalities to compare with independent copies
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be the left-hand side. Since $0=\bbe_y f(y)$ we have, by the triangle inequality, and H\"{o}lder's inequality, \begin{align} S & = \bbe_{x_1, \dots, x_n}\left\lvert \sum_i f(x_i) - \bbe_{y_i} f(y_i)\right\rvert^{2m} \\ & = \bbe_{x_1, \dots, x_n} \left\lvert\bbe_{y_i}\brac{\sum_i f(x_i) - f(y_i)}\right\rvert^{2m} \\ & \le \bbe_{x_1,\dots,y_n} \left\lvert \sum_i f(x_i) - f(y_i)\right\rvert^{2m} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Centre the sum and apply the triangle and Hölder inequalities to compare with independent copies.

nodes.name: Symmetrise with random signs $\epsilon_i$
nodes.statement: Changing the role of $x_i$ and $y_i$ makes no difference here, but multiplies the $i$ summand by $\{-1,+1\}$, and therefore for any $\epsilon_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, \[ S \leq\bbe_{x_1,\ldots,y_n}\left\lvert \sum_i \epsilon_i(f(x_i)-f(y_i))\right\rvert^{2m}.\] In particular, if we sample $\epsilon_i\in\{-1,+1\}$ uniformly at random, then \[ S \leq\bbe_{\epsilon_i} \bbe_{x_1,\ldots,y_n}\left\lvert \sum_i \epsilon_i(f(x_i)-f(y_i))\right\rvert^{2m}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrise with random signs $\epsilon_i$.

nodes.name: Fix $z_i$ and expand the $2m$-th moment over the signs
nodes.statement: We now change the order of expectation and consider the expectation over just $\epsilon_i$, viewing the $f(x_i)-f(y_i)=z_i$, say, as fixed quantities. For any $z_i$ we can expand $\bbe_{\epsilon_i} \lvert \sum_i \epsilon_iz_i\rvert^{2m}$ and then bound it from above, using the triangle inequality and $\abs{z_i}\leq 4$, by \[4^{2m}\sum_{k_1+\cdots+k_n=2m}\binom{2m}{k_1,\ldots,k_n}\abs{\bbe\epsilon_1^{k_1}\cdots \epsilon_n^{k_n}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Fix $z_i$ and expand the $2m$-th moment over the signs.

nodes.name: Only even exponents survive; bound the multinomial count by $m^mn^m$
nodes.statement: The inner expectation vanishes unless each $k_i$ is even, when it is trivially one. Therefore the above quantity is exactly \[\sum_{l_1+\cdots+l_n=m}\binom{2m}{2l_1,\ldots,2l_n}\leq m^mn^m,\] since for any $l_1+\cdots+l_n=m$, \[\binom{2m}{2l_1,\ldots,2l_n}\leq m^m\binom{m}{l_1,\ldots,l_n}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Only even exponents survive; bound the multinomial count by $m^mn^m$.

nodes.name: Verify the multinomial inequality via factorials
nodes.statement: This can be seen, for example, by writing both sides out using factorials, yielding \[\frac{(2m)!}{(2l_1)!\cdots (2l_n)!}\leq \frac{(2m)!}{2^mm!}\frac{m!}{l_1!\cdots l_n!}\leq m^m\frac{m!}{l_1!\cdots l_n!}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Verify the multinomial inequality via factorials.

nodes.name: A random translate has mean $\mu_A\ast f(x)$
nodes.statement: Note that if $a\in A$ is chosen uniformly at random then, for any fixed $x\in G$, \[\bbe f(x-a_i)= \frac{1}{\abs{A}}\sum_{a\in A}f(x-a)=\frac{1}{\abs{A}}\ind{A}\ast f(x)=\mu_A\ast f(x).\]
nodes.statement_short: A random translate has mean $\mu_A\ast f(x)$.

nodes.name: Apply the Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequality pointwise in $x$
nodes.statement: Therefore, if we choose $a_1,\ldots,a_k\in A$ independently uniformly at random, for any fixed $x\in G$ and $1\leq i\leq k$, the random variable $f(x-a_i)-f\ast \mu_A(x)$ has mean zero. By the Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequality Lemma~\ref{mzi}, therefore, \begin{multline*} \bbe\abs{ \frac{1}{k}\sum_i f(x-a_i)-f\ast \mu_A(x)}^{2m} \leq \\(16m/k)^mk^{-1} \bbe \sum_i \abs{f(x-a_i)-f\ast \mu_A(x)}^{2m}. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequality pointwise in $x$.

nodes.name: Sum over $x$ and split with the triangle inequality
nodes.statement: We now sum both sides over all $x\in G$. By the triangle inequality, for any fixed $1\leq i\leq k$ and $a_i\in A$, \begin{align*} \sum_{x\in G} \abs{f(x-a_i)-f\ast \mu_A(x)}^{2m} &\leq 2^{2m-1}\sum_{x\in G}\abs{f(x-a_i)}^{2m}+\sum_{x\in G}\abs{f\ast \mu_A(x)}^{2m}\\ &\leq 2^{2m-1}\brac{\norm{f}_{2m}^{2m}+\norm{f\ast \mu_A}_{2m}^{2m}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $x$ and split with the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Young's inequality bounds $\|f\ast\mu_A\|_{2m}$ by $\|f\|_{2m}$
nodes.statement:
We note that $
orm{\mu_A}_1= rac{1}{\abs{A}}\sum_{x\in A}\ind{A}(x)=\abs{A}/\abs{A}=1$, and hence by Young's inequality, $
orm{f\ast \mu_A}_{2m}\leq 
orm{f}_{2m}$, and so \[\sum_{x\in G} \abs{f(x-a_i)-f\ast \mu_A(x)}^{2m}\leq 2^{2m}
orm{f}_{2m}^{2m}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Young's inequality bounds $\|f\ast\mu_A\|_{2m}$ by $\|f\|_{2m}$.

nodes.name: Fix $t$, define $F$ and write the difference as $F\ast\mu_C$
nodes.statement: Fix $t\in T$ and let $F=\tau_t(\mu_A\ast 1_B)-\mu_A\ast 1_B$. We have, for any $x\in G$, \[(\tau_t(\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C)-\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C)(x)=F\ast \mu_C(x)=\sum_y F(y)\mu_{C}(x-y)=\sum_yF(y)\mu_{x-C}(y).\]
nodes.statement_short: Fix $t$, define $F$ and write the difference as $F\ast\mu_C$.

nodes.name: Hölder's inequality against $\mu_{x-C}$
nodes.statement: By Hölder's inequality, this is (in absolute value), for any $m\geq 1$, \[\norm{F}_{2m}\norm{\mu_{x-C}}_{1+\frac{1}{2m-1}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Hölder's inequality against $\mu_{x-C}$.

nodes.name: Bound both factors by construction of $T$ and direct calculation
nodes.statement: By the construction of $T$ the first factor is at most $\frac{\epsilon}{e}\| 1_B\|_{2m}=\frac{\epsilon}{e}\lvert B\rvert^{1/2m}$. We have by calculation \[\norm{\mu_{x-C}}_{1+\frac{1}{2m-1}}=\lvert x-C\rvert^{-1/2m}=\lvert C\rvert^{-1/2m}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Bound both factors by construction of $T$ and direct calculation.

nodes.name: Combine into an $L^\infty$ bound with $(|C|/|B|)^{-1/2m}$
nodes.statement: Therefore we have shown that \[\| \tau_t(\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C)-\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C\|_{\infty}\leq \frac{\epsilon}{e}(\lvert C\rvert/\lvert B\rvert)^{-1/2m}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine into an $L^\infty$ bound with $(|C|/|B|)^{-1/2m}$.

nodes.name: Choice of $m$ makes $(|C|/|B|)^{-1/2m}\le e$
nodes.statement: The claim now follows since, by choice of $m$, \[(\lvert C\rvert/\lvert B\rvert)^{-1/2m}\leq e\] (dividing into cases as to whether $\eta=1$ or not).
nodes.statement_short: Choice of $m$ makes $(|C|/|B|)^{-1/2m}\le e$.

nodes.name: Take $T$ from $L_\infty$ almost periodicity with $\epsilon/k$
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be as in Theorem~\ref{linfty_ap} with $\epsilon$ replaced by $\epsilon/k$.
nodes.statement_short: Take $T$ from $L_\infty$ almost periodicity with $\epsilon/k$.

nodes.name: Expand the $k$-fold convolution as an average of translates
nodes.statement: Note that, for any $x\in G$, \[\mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C(x)=\frac{1}{\lvert T\rvert^k}\sum_{t_1,\ldots,t_k\in T}\tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_k}\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C(x).\]
nodes.statement_short: Expand the $k$-fold convolution as an average of translates.

nodes.name: Reduce to a single shift by $t_1+\cdots+t_k$
nodes.statement: It therefore suffices (by the triangle inequality) to show, for any fixed $x\in G$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_k\in T$, that with $F=\mu_A\ast 1_B\ast \mu_C$, we have \[\lvert \tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_k}F(x)-F(x)\rvert \leq \epsilon.\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a single shift by $t_1+\cdots+t_k$.

nodes.name: Telescope into $k$ single-step shifts
nodes.statement: This follows by the triangle inequality applied $k$ times if we knew that, for $1\leq l\leq k$, \[\lvert \tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_l}F(x)-\tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_{l-1}}F(x)\rvert \leq \epsilon/k.\]
nodes.statement_short: Telescope into $k$ single-step shifts.

nodes.name: Rewrite each step as a single translate difference
nodes.statement: We can write the left-hand side as \[\lvert \tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_l}F(x)-\tau_{t_1+\cdots+t_{l-1}}F(x)\rvert=\lvert \tau_{t_l}F(x-t_1-\cdots-t-{l-1})-F(x-t_1-\cdots-t-{l-1})\rvert.\]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite each step as a single translate difference.

nodes.name: Bounded by $\|\tau_{t_l}F-F\|_\infty$, done by choice of $T$
nodes.statement: The right-hand side is at most \[\| \tau_{t_l}F-F\|_\infty\] and we are done by choice of $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded by $\|\tau_{t_l}F-F\|_\infty$, done by choice of $T$.

nodes.statement_short: Cover the circle by few small discs and define the coordinate map $f$.

nodes.name: Pigeonhole gives a large fibre $B'$
nodes.statement: By the pigeonhole principle there must exist some $(j_1,\ldots,j_{d})$ such that $f^{-1}(j_1,\ldots,j_d)$ has size at least $(\lceil 2/\rho\rceil)^{-\mathrm{rk}(\nu)}\abs{\mathrm{Bohr}(\nu)}$. Call this set $B'$.
nodes.statement_short: Pigeonhole gives a large fibre $B'$.

nodes.name: Fix $x\in B'$ and reduce to showing $B'-x$ lies in the dilate
nodes.statement: It must be non-empty, so fix some $x\in B'$. We claim that $B'-x\subseteq \abs{\mathrm{Bohr}(\rho\cdot \nu)}$, which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $x\in B'$ and reduce to showing $B'-x$ lies in the dilate.

nodes.name: Two points of a fibre share a disc centre for each $\gamma$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $z=x+y$ with $x,y\in B'$, and fix some $\gamma\in \Gamma$. By assumption there is some $z_j\in \mathbb{C}$ such that $\lvert z_j-\gamma(x)\rvert \leq \rho \nu(\gamma)/2$ and $\lvert z_j-\gamma(y)\rvert \leq \rho \nu(\gamma)/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Two points of a fibre share a disc centre for each $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality puts the difference in $\mathrm{Bohr}(\rho\cdot\nu)$
nodes.statement: Then by the triangle inequality, \[\lvert 1-\gamma(y-x)\rvert=\lvert \gamma(x)-\gamma(y)\rvert \leq \rho \nu(\gamma)\] and so $z=y-x\in \mathrm{Bohr}(\rho\cdot \nu)$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality puts the difference in $\mathrm{Bohr}(\rho\cdot\nu)$.

nodes.name: Convexity bound $e^{tx}\le\cosh x+t\sinh x$
nodes.statement: Using the convexity of $t\mapsto e^{tx}$ (for all $x\geq 0$ and $t\in[-1,1]$) we have \[e^{tx}\le \cosh(x)+t\sinh(x).\]
nodes.statement_short: Convexity bound $e^{tx}\le\cosh x+t\sinh x$.

nodes.name: Specialise to complex $z$
nodes.statement: It follows (taking $x=\lvert z\rvert$ and $t=\Re(z)/\lvert z\rvert$) that, for any $z\in \mathbb{C}$, \[e^{\Re z}\le \cosh \lvert z\rvert +\Re(z/\lvert z\rvert)\sinh \lvert z\rvert.\]
nodes.statement_short: Specialise to complex $z$.

nodes.name: Apply pointwise to the Fourier expansion of $f$ as a product
nodes.statement: In particular, if $c_\gamma\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\lvert c_\gamma\rvert=1$ is such that $\widehat{f}(\gamma)=c_\gamma\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert$, then \begin{align*} e^{\Re f(x)} &= \exp\left( \Re \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\widehat{f}(\gamma)\gamma(x)\right)\\ &=\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma} \exp\left( \Re \widehat{f}(\gamma)\gamma(x)\right)\\ &\le \prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma}\left( \cosh \lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert +\Re c_\gamma \gamma(x)\sinh \lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply pointwise to the Fourier expansion of $f$ as a product.

nodes.name: Average the product bound over $x$
nodes.statement: Therefore \[\E_x e^{\Re f(x)}\le \E_x \prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma} \left( \cosh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert+\Re c_\gamma \gamma(x)\sinh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right).\]
nodes.statement_short: Average the product bound over $x$.

nodes.name: Expand the product over partitions of $\Gamma$ into three parts
nodes.statement: Using $\Re z=(z+\overline{z})/2$ the product here can be expanded as the sum of \[\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2}\frac{c_\gamma}{2}\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_3}\frac{\overline{c_\gamma}}{2}\left(\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_1}\cosh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right)\left(\prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2\cup\Gamma_3}\sinh\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert\right)\left(\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2}\gamma-\sum_{\lambda\in \Gamma_3}\lambda\right)(x)\] as $\Gamma_1\sqcup \Gamma_2\sqcup \Gamma_3=\Gamma$ ranges over all partitions of $\Gamma$ into three disjoint parts.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the product over partitions of $\Gamma$ into three parts.

nodes.name: Dissociativity kills all cross terms on averaging
nodes.statement: Using the definition of dissociativity we see that \[\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma_2}\gamma-\sum_{\lambda\in \Gamma_3}\lambda\neq 0\] unless $\Gamma_2=\Gamma_3=\emptyset$. In particular summing this term over all $x\in G$ gives $0$. Therefore the only term that survives averaging over $x$ is when $\Gamma_1=\Gamma$, and so \[\E_x e^{\Re f(x)}\le \prod_{\gamma\in \Gamma} \cosh \lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert.\]
nodes.statement_short: Dissociativity kills all cross terms on averaging.

nodes.name: Use $\cosh x\le e^{x^2/2}$ and Parseval; apply to $\pm f$ for the second claim
nodes.statement: The conclusion now follows using $\cosh(x) \le e^{x^2/2}$ and $\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma}\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert^2=\| f\|_2^2$. The second conclusion follows by applying it to $f(x)$ and $-f(x)$ and using \[e^{\abs{y}}\le e^y+e^{-y}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Use $\cosh x\le e^{x^2/2}$ and Parseval; apply to $\pm f$ for the second claim.

nodes.name: Reduce to bounding the real part
nodes.statement:
It is enough to show that $
orm{\Re f}_p \le 2\sqrt{pe} 
orm f_2$ as then $$
orm{f}_p \le 
orm{\Re f}_p + 
orm{i \Im f}_p = 
orm{\Re f}_p + 
orm{\Re (-if)}_p \le 4\sqrt{pe} 
orm f_2$$
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounding the real part.

nodes.name: WLOG $f\neq 0$ and normalise $\|f\|_2=\sqrt p$
nodes.statement:
If $f = 0$, the result is obvious. So assume $f 
e 0$. $
orm{f}_2 > 0$, so WLOG $
orm{f}_2 = \sqrt p$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $f\neq 0$ and normalise $\|f\|_2=\sqrt p$.

nodes.name: Apply Rudin's exponential inequality with $x^p/p!\le e^x$
nodes.statement: Rudin's exponential inequality for $f$ becomes $\E \exp|\Re f| \le 2\exp(\frac p 2) = (2\sqrt e)^p$. Using $\frac{x^p}{p!} \le e^x$ for positive $x$, we get $$\frac{\norm{\Re f}_p^p}{p^p} \le \frac{\norm{\Re f}_p^p}{p!} = \E \frac{|\Re f|^p}{p!} \le \E \exp|\Re f|$$
nodes.statement_short: Apply Rudin's exponential inequality with $x^p/p!\le e^x$.

nodes.name: Rearrange to the stated bound
nodes.statement: Rearranging, $\norm{\Re f}_p \le 2 p\sqrt{e} = 2 \sqrt{pe} \norm f_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange to the stated bound.

nodes.name: Sum the large-spectrum lower bounds over $\Delta$
nodes.statement: By definition of $\Delta_\eta(f)$ we know that \[\eta\norm{f}_1\abs{\Delta}\le \sum_{\gamma\in\Delta} \lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert.\]
nodes.statement_short: Sum the large-spectrum lower bounds over $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Choose unimodular phases $c_\gamma$
nodes.statement: There exists some $c_\gamma\in\bbc$ with $\lvert c_\gamma\rvert=1$ for all $\gamma$ such that \[\lvert \widehat{f}(\gamma)\rvert=c_\gamma\widehat{f}(\gamma)=c_\gamma \sum_{x\in G}f(x)\overline{\gamma(x)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose unimodular phases $c_\gamma$.

nodes.name: Interchange sums
nodes.statement: Interchanging the sums, therefore, \[\eta\norm{f}_1\abs{\Delta}\le \sum_{x\in G}f(x)\sum_{\gamma\in\Delta} c_\gamma \overline{\gamma(x)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Interchange sums.

nodes.name: Hölder's inequality, then take $m$-th powers
nodes.statement: By H\"{o}lder's inequality the right-hand side is at most \[\brac{\sum_x \abs{f(x)}}^{1-1/m}\brac{\sum_x \abs{f(x)}\abs{\sum_{\gamma\in\Delta}c_\gamma\overline{\gamma(x)}}^m}^{1/m}.\] Taking $m$th powers, therefore, we have \[\eta^m\abs{\Delta}^m\norm{f}_1\le \sum_{x}\abs{f(x)}\abs{\sum_{\gamma\in\Delta}c_\gamma\overline{\gamma(x)}}^m.\]
nodes.statement_short: Hölder's inequality, then take $m$-th powers.

nodes.name: Insert $\nu$ and apply Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
By assumption we can bound $\abs{f(x)}\le \abs{f(x)}
u(x)^{1/2}$, and therefore by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality the right-hand side is bounded above by \[
orm{f}_2 rac{\sum_x 
u(x)\abs{\sum_{\gamma\in\Delta}c_\gamma\overline{\gamma(x)}}^{2m}}^{1/2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Insert $\nu$ and apply Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Square and simplify
nodes.statement_short: Square and simplify.

nodes.name: Expand the power and rewrite as Fourier coefficients of $\nu$
nodes.statement: Expanding out the power, the right-hand side is equal to \[\sum_x \nu(x)\sum_{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}}c_{\gamma_1}\cdots \overline{c_{\gamma_{2m}}} (\overline{\gamma_1}\cdots \gamma_{2m})(x).\] Changing the order of summation this is equal to \[\sum_{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}}c_{\gamma_1}\cdots \overline{c_{\gamma_{2m}}} \widehat{\nu}(\gamma_1\cdots \overline{\gamma_{2m}}).\]
nodes.statement_short: Expand the power and rewrite as Fourier coefficients of $\nu$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality gives the weighted energy
nodes.statement: The result follows by the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality gives the weighted energy.

nodes.name: Take a maximal dissociated subset $A'$, of size at most $K$
nodes.statement: Let $A'\subseteq A$ be a maximal dissociated subset (this exists and is non-empty, since trivially any singleton is dissociated). We have $\abs{A'}\le K$ by assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal dissociated subset $A'$, of size at most $K$.

nodes.name: Any $x\notin A'$ breaks dissociativity of $A'\cup\{x\}$, giving two equal subset sums
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be the span on the right-hand side. It is obvious that $A'\subseteq S$. Suppose that $x\in A\backslash A'$. Then $A'\cup\{x\}$ is not dissociated by maximality. Therefore there exists some $y\in G$ and two distinct sets $B,C\subseteq A'\cup \{x\}$ such that \[\sum_{b\in B}b = y = \sum_{c\in C} c.\]
nodes.statement_short: Any $x\notin A'$ breaks dissociativity of $A'\cup\{x\}$, giving two equal subset sums.

nodes.name: Case $x$ in neither set contradicts dissociativity
nodes.statement: If $x\not\in B$ and $x\not\in C$ then this contradicts the dissociativity of $A'$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $x$ in neither set contradicts dissociativity.

nodes.name: Case $x$ in both sets also contradicts dissociativity
nodes.statement: If $x\in B$ and $x\in C$ then we have \[\sum_{b\in B\backslash x}b=y-x=\sum_{c\in C\backslash x}c,\] again contradicting the dissociativity of $A'$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $x$ in both sets also contradicts dissociativity.

nodes.name: So $x$ is a signed sum of elements of $A'$
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, therefore, $x\in B$ and $x\not\in C$. Therefore \[x=\sum_{c\in C}c - \sum_{b\in B\backslash x}b\] which is in the span as required.
nodes.statement_short: So $x$ is a signed sum of elements of $A'$.

nodes.name: Reduce to showing the spectrum has no dissociated set of size $K$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{diss_span} it suffices to show that $\Delta_\eta(f)$ contains no dissociated set with at least \[K= \lceil e\mathcal{L}(\alpha)\eta^{-2}\rceil+1\] many elements.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing the spectrum has no dissociated set of size $K$.

nodes.name: Suppose a dissociated $\Delta$ of size $K$ exists
nodes.statement: Suppose not, and let $\Delta\subseteq \Delta_\eta(f)$ be a dissociated set of size $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose a dissociated $\Delta$ of size $K$ exists.

nodes.name: Upper bound on its energy
nodes.statement: Then by Lemma~\ref{diss_energy} we have, for any $m\geq 1$, \[E_{2m}(\Delta)\le m!K^m.\]
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound on its energy.

nodes.name: Lower bound on its energy
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by Lemma~\ref{spec_hoelder}, \[\eta^{2m}\alpha K^{2m}\le E_{2m}(\Delta).\]
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound on its energy.

nodes.name: Combine the bounds
nodes.statement: Rearranging these bounds, we have \[K^m \le m! \alpha^{-1}\eta^{-2m}\le m^m\alpha^{-1}\eta^{-2m}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine the bounds.

nodes.name: Choose $m=\mathcal{L}(\alpha)$ for a contradiction
nodes.statement: Therefore $K\le \alpha^{-1/m}m\eta^{-2}$. This is a contradiction to the choice of $K$ if we choose $m=\mathcal{L}(\alpha)$, since $\alpha^{-1/m}\le e$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $m=\mathcal{L}(\alpha)$ for a contradiction.

nodes.name: Dispose of the trivial case of zero norm
nodes.statement: First note that the statement is trivially true (with $A_1=B_1$ and $A_2=B_2$, say) if $\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p=0$. We can therefore assume this is $\neq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Dispose of the trivial case of zero norm.

nodes.name: Define $A_i(s)$ and rewrite the moment as a sum over $s$
nodes.statement: For $s\in G^{p}$ let $A_1(s)=B_1\cap (A+s_1)\cap\cdots\cap (A+s_{p})$, and similarly for $A_2(s)$. Note that \begin{align*} \langle (\ind{A}\circ \ind{A})^p, f\rangle_\mu &=\sum_{x} \mu_{B_1}\circ \mu_{B_2}(x)(\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}(x))^pf(x)\\ &=\sum_{b_1,b_2}\mu_{B_1}(b_1)\mu_{B_2}(b_2)\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}(b_1-b_2)^{p}f(b_1-b_2)\\ &=\sum_{b_1,b_2}\mu_{B_1}(b_1)\mu_{B_2}(b_2)\brac{\sum_{t\in G}\ind{A+t}(b_1)\ind{A+t}(b_2)}^{p}f(b_1-b_2)\\ &=\sum_{b_1,b_2}\mu_{B_1}(b_1)\mu_{B_2}(b_2)\sum_{s\in G^p}\ind{A_1(s)}(b_1)\ind{A_2(s)}(b_2)f(b_1-b_2)\\ &=\abs{B_1}^{-1}\abs{B_2}^{-1}\sum_{s\in G^p}\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)}, f\rangle. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $A_i(s)$ and rewrite the moment as a sum over $s$.

nodes.name: Specialise to $f\equiv 1$ and define the ratio $\eta$
nodes.statement: In particular, applying this with $f\equiv 1$ we see that \[\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p=\abs{B_1}^{-1}\abs{B_2}^{-1}\sum_s\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}\] and \[\frac{\langle (\ind{A}\circ \ind{A})^p,f\rangle_\mu}{\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p}=\frac{\sum_{s}\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)}, f\rangle}{\sum_s \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}}=\eta,\] say.
nodes.statement_short: Specialise to $f\equiv 1$ and define the ratio $\eta$.

nodes.name: Introduce threshold $M$ and indicator $g$ of small pairs; state a strict inequality
nodes.statement: Let $M>0$ be some parameter, and let \[g(s) = \begin{cases} 1&\textrm{ if }0<\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}<M^2\textrm{ and }\\0&\textrm{ otherwise.}\end{cases}\] Then we have \[\sum_s g(s)\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)} <\sum_s M\abs{A_1(s)}^{1/2}\abs{A_2(s)}^{1/2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce threshold $M$ and indicator $g$ of small pairs; state a strict inequality.

nodes.name: Reduce to finding one strictly smaller summand
nodes.statement: To see why, note first that each summand on the left-hand side is $\leq$ the corresponding summand on the right-hand side, arguing by cases on whether $g(s)=1$ or not. It therefore suffices to show that there exists some $s$ such that the summand on the left-hand side is $<$ the corresponding summand on the right-hand side.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to finding one strictly smaller summand.

nodes.name: Case $g\equiv 0$
nodes.statement: If $g(s)=0$ for all $s$ then choose some $s$ such that $\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}\geq M^2$ (this must exist or else $\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}=0$ for all $s$, but then $\norm{1_A\circ 1_A}_{p(\mu)}^p=0$ by the above calculation).
nodes.statement_short: Case $g\equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Case some $g(s)=1$
nodes.statement: Otherwise, choose some $s$ such that $g(s)=1$, and note that for this $s$ we have, by definition of $s$, \[\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}<M\abs{A_1(s)}^{1/2}\abs{A_2(s)}^{1/2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Case some $g(s)=1$.

nodes.name: Choose $M$; Cauchy-Schwarz shows the large pairs carry over half the mass
nodes.statement: We now choose \[M=\tfrac{1}{2}\abs{A}^{-p}(\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2})^{1/2}\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p,\] so that, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, \begin{align*} \sum_s g(s)\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)} &< M \sum_s \abs{A_1(s)}^{1/2}\abs{A_2(s)}^{1/2}\\ &\leq M\brac{\sum_s \sum_{x\in G}1_{A_1(s)}(x)}^{1/2}\brac{\sum_s \sum_{x\in G}1_{A_2(s)}(x)}^{1/2}\\ &= M\abs{A}^p(\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2})^{1/2}\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\sum_s \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)} \end{align*} and so \[ \sum_s (1-g(s))\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)} > \frac{1}{2}\sum_s \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}\] whence \[\sum_s\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)},f\rangle =\eta \sum \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)} < 2\eta \sum_s \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}(1-g(s)).\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose $M$; Cauchy-Schwarz shows the large pairs carry over half the mass.

nodes.name: Select a good $s$ by averaging
nodes.statement: In particular there must exist some $s$ such that \[\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)},f\rangle< 2\eta \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}(1-g(s)).\]
nodes.statement_short: Select a good $s$ by averaging.

nodes.name: Verify both requirements for this $s$
nodes.statement: We claim this $s$ meets the requirements. The first is satisfied since the right-hand side is $\leq 2\eta \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}$. The second is satisfied since the left-hand side is trivially $\geq 0$ and hence such an $s$ must satisfy $g(s)=0$, whence either $ \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}\geq M^2$, that is, \[\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}\geq \frac{1}{4}\abs{A}^{-2p}\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2}\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^{2p},\] or $\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}=0$, which can't happen because then the right-hand side is $=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Verify both requirements for this $s$.

nodes.name: First requirement from $1-g(s)\le 1$
nodes.statement: The first is satisfied since the right-hand side is $\leq 2\eta \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}$.
nodes.statement_short: First requirement from $1-g(s)\le 1$.

nodes.name: Second requirement since $g(s)=0$ forces large $|A_1(s)||A_2(s)|$
nodes.statement: The second is satisfied since the left-hand side is trivially $\geq 0$ and hence such an $s$ must satisfy $g(s)=0$, whence either $ \abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}\geq M^2$, that is, \[\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}\geq \frac{1}{4}\abs{A}^{-2p}\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2}\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^{2p},\] or $\abs{A_1(s)}\abs{A_2(s)}=0$, which can't happen because then the right-hand side is $=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Second requirement since $g(s)=0$ forces large $|A_1(s)||A_2(s)|$.

nodes.name: Pass from the product to the minimum
nodes.statement: The final bound now follows since $xy \leq \min(x,y)$ when $x,y\leq 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass from the product to the minimum.

nodes.name: Apply dependent random choice with $f=1_{G\setminus S}$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{drc} with $f=\ind{G\backslash S}$. This produces some $A_1\subseteq B_1$ and $A_2\subseteq B_2$ such that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2}, \ind{G\backslash S}\rangle\leq 2\frac{\langle (\ind{A}\circ \ind{A})^p,\ind{G\backslash S}\rangle_\mu}{\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p}\] and \[\min\brac{\frac{\abs{A_1}}{\abs{B_1}},\frac{\abs{A_2}}{\abs{B_2}}}\geq \frac{1}{4}\abs{A}^{-2p}\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^{2p}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply dependent random choice with $f=1_{G\setminus S}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to bounding the moment on the complement of $S$ by definition of $S$
nodes.statement: It then suffices to note that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle=1-\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{G\backslash S}\rangle\] and by definition of $S$ we have \[\langle (\ind{A}\circ \ind{A})^p,\ind{G\backslash S}\rangle_\mu\leq (1-\epsilon)^p\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p\sum_{x}\mu(x)=(1-\epsilon)^p\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p.\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounding the moment on the complement of $S$ by definition of $S$.

nodes.name: Use $p\ge\epsilon^{-1}\log(2/\delta)$ and $1-x\le e^{-x}$
nodes.statement: Now use the fact that $p\geq \epsilon^{-1}\log(2/\delta)$ together with the inequality $1-x\leq e^{-x}$ to deduce that the right-hand side is $\leq \tfrac{\delta}{2}\norm{\ind{A}\circ \ind{A}}_{p(\mu)}^p$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $p\ge\epsilon^{-1}\log(2/\delta)$ and $1-x\le e^{-x}$.

nodes.name: Set $k$ and note the small-doubling and density hypotheses
nodes.statement: (In this proof we write $G=\mathbb{F}_q^n$.) Let $k=\lceil \lo(\epsilon\alpha/4)\rceil$. Note that $\lvert A_1+G\rvert=\lvert G\rvert\leq \alpha^{-1}\lvert A\rvert$. Furthermore, $\lvert A_2\rvert/\lvert S\rvert\geq \alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Set $k$ and note the small-doubling and density hypotheses.

nodes.name: Boosted $L_\infty$ almost periodicity gives $T$
nodes.statement: Therefore by Theorem~\ref{linfty_ap_boosted} there exists some $T\subseteq G$ with \[\lvert T\rvert \geq \exp(-2^{16}\lo(\alpha)^2k^2\epsilon^{-2})\lvert S\rvert\] such that \[\| \mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}-\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}\|_{\infty}\leq \epsilon/4.\]
nodes.statement_short: Boosted $L_\infty$ almost periodicity gives $T$.

nodes.name: Define $V$ as the annihilator of the large spectrum of $\mu_T$ and rewrite both inner products
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta=\Delta_{1/2}(\mu_T)$ and \[V = \{ x \in G : \gamma(x)=1\textrm{ for all }\gamma\in\Delta\}.\] Note that \[\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle = \langle \mu_V,\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}\rangle=\frac{1}{\abs{V}}\sum_{v\in V}\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)\] and \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle = \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ\ind{S}(0).\]
nodes.statement_short: Define $V$ as the annihilator of the large spectrum of $\mu_T$ and rewrite both inner products.

nodes.name: Bound the difference by an average over $v\in V$
nodes.statement: Therefore \[\abs{\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle-\langle \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle}\leq \frac{1}{\abs{V}}\sum_{v\in V}\abs{\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)-\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(0)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the difference by an average over $v\in V$.

nodes.name: Reduce to a pointwise bound for $v\in V$
nodes.statement: In particular it suffices to show that, for any $v\in V$, \[\abs{\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)-\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(0)}\leq \epsilon.\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a pointwise bound for $v\in V$.

nodes.name: Reduce further to the $\mu_T^{(k)}$-smoothed version
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality and construction of $T$, it suffices to show that \[\abs{\mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(v)-\mu_T^{(k)}\ast\mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(0)}\leq \epsilon/2.\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce further to the $\mu_T^{(k)}$-smoothed version.

nodes.name: Fourier expansion of the smoothed function
nodes.statement: By the Fourier transform we have, for any $x\in G$, \[\mu_T^{(k)}\ast \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \ind{S}(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma\in \widehat{G}}\widehat{\mu_T}(\gamma)^k\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)\gamma(x).\]
nodes.statement_short: Fourier expansion of the smoothed function.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality on the Fourier side
nodes.statement: Therefore the left-hand side of the desired inequality is, by the triangle inequality, at most \[\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma\in \widehat{G}}\abs{\widehat{\mu_T}(\gamma)}^k\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)}\abs{\gamma(v)-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality on the Fourier side.

nodes.name: Terms in $\Delta$ vanish; others are bounded by $2^{1-k}$
nodes.statement: By choice of $v\in V$ the summand vanishes when $\gamma\in\Delta$. When $\gamma\not\in \Delta$ the summand is bounded above by \[2^{1-k}\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Terms in $\Delta$ vanish; others are bounded by $2^{1-k}$.

nodes.name: Sum and use the trivial bound on $\widehat{1_S}$
nodes.statement: Therefore the left-hand side of the desired inequality is at most \[2^{1-k}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma}\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)\widehat{\ind{-S}}(\gamma)}\leq 2^{1-k}\abs{S}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\gamma}\abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}(\gamma)\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}(\gamma)}\] using the trivial bound $\lvert\widehat{\ind{S}}\rvert\leq \abs{S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum and use the trivial bound on $\widehat{1_S}$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and Parseval bound the sum by $\alpha^{-1}$, giving the inequality
nodes.statement: By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality the sum on the right is at most \[\brac{\sum_\gamma \abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_1}}}^2}^{1/2}\brac{\sum_\gamma \abs{\widehat{\mu_{A_2}}}^2}^{1/2}.\] By Parseval's identity this is at most $\alpha^{-1}$. Therefore the desired inequality follows from \[2^{1-k}\abs{S}\frac{1}{N}\alpha^{-1}\leq 2^{1-k}\alpha^{-1}\leq \epsilon/2.\]
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz and Parseval bound the sum by $\alpha^{-1}$, giving the inequality.

nodes.name: Turn to the codimension of $V$
nodes.statement: It remains to check the codimension of $V$.
nodes.statement_short: Turn to the codimension of $V$.

nodes.name: Apply Chang's lemma to the spectrum
nodes.statement: For this, let $\Delta'\subseteq \Delta$ be as provided by Chang's lemma, Lemma~\ref{chang}, so that \[\Delta\subseteq \left\{ \sum_{\gamma\in\Delta'}c_\gamma \gamma : c_\gamma\in \{-1,0,1\} \right\}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Chang's lemma to the spectrum.

nodes.name: Define $W\le V$ and bound its codimension via Chang's bound
nodes.statement: Let \[W= \{ x \in G : \gamma(x)=1\textrm{ for all }\gamma\in\Delta'\}.\] It follows that $W\leq V$, so it suffices to bound the codimension of $W$. This we can bound trivially using the bound from Chang's lemma and the fact that $\lo(\delta)=\log(e^2/\delta)\leq 2+\log(1/\delta)\leq 4\log(1/\delta)$, provided $\log(1/\delta)\geq 1$, so \[\abs{\Delta'}\leq \lceil 4e\mathcal{L}(\delta)\rceil\leq 2^7\log(1/\delta),\] where \[\delta=\abs{T}/N\geq \exp(-2^{16}\lo(\alpha)^2k^2\epsilon^{-2}),\] so \[\mathrm{codim}(V)\leq \abs{\Delta'}\leq 2^{23}\lo(\alpha)^2k^2\epsilon^{-2}\leq 2^{25}\lo(\alpha)^2\lo(\epsilon \alpha/4)^2\epsilon^{-2},\] and now use $\lo(\epsilon\alpha/4)\leq 2\lo(\epsilon\alpha)$, say.
nodes.statement_short: Define $W\le V$ and bound its codimension via Chang's bound.

nodes.name: Hölder's inequality bounds the deviation by the $L^p$ norm of $\mu_A\ast\mu_A-1/N$
nodes.statement: By H\"{o}lder's inequality, for any $p\geq 1$ \[\epsilon < \abs{ N\langle \mu_A \ast \mu_A - 1/N, \mu_C \rangle } \leq \norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1/N}_p\gamma^{-1/p}N^{1-1/p}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Hölder's inequality bounds the deviation by the $L^p$ norm of $\mu_A\ast\mu_A-1/N$.

nodes.name: Choose $p=2\lceil\mathcal{L}(\gamma)\rceil$ to get a lower bound on $\|f\ast f\|_p$
nodes.statement: In particular if we choose $p=2\lceil\lo(\gamma)\rceil$ then $\gamma^{-1/p}\leq e^{1/2}\leq 2$ and so we deduce that, by Lemma~\ref{ast_expand}, \[\norm{f\ast f}_{p}\geq \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon N^{1/p-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose $p=2\lceil\mathcal{L}(\gamma)\rceil$ to get a lower bound on $\|f\ast f\|_p$.

nodes.name: Pass to $f\circ f$ and the normalised norm
nodes.statement: It remains to use Lemmas~\ref{ast_expand} and \ref{circ_expand} and apply Lemma~\ref{ast_le_circ}, and note that we can pass from the $L^p$ norm to the $L^p(\mu)$ norm losing a factor of $N^{1/p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to $f\circ f$ and the normalised norm.

nodes.name: Global dichotomy gives a large $L^p(\mu)$ norm of $f\circ f$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{global_dichotomy}, if $f=\mu_A-1/N$, \[\norm{f\circ f}_{p(\mu)}\geq \epsilon /2N,\] where $p=2\lceil \lo(\gamma)\rceil\leq 4\lo(\gamma)$.
nodes.statement_short: Global dichotomy gives a large $L^p(\mu)$ norm of $f\circ f$.

nodes.name: Unbalancing gives a $p'$-norm increment
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{unbalancing} there exists some $p'$ such that \[p'\leq 128\epsilon^{-1}\log(96/\epsilon)\lo(\gamma)\] such that \[\norm{f\circ f+1/N}_{p'(\mu)}\geq (1+\epsilon/4)/N.\]
nodes.statement_short: Unbalancing gives a $p'$-norm increment.

nodes.name: Identify $f\circ f+1/N$ with $\mu_A\circ\mu_A$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{circ_expand} $f\circ f+1/N=\mu_A\circ \mu_A$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $f\circ f+1/N$ with $\mu_A\circ\mu_A$.

nodes.name: Sifting corollary gives dense $A_1,A_2$ concentrated on $S$
nodes.statement: Let $q=2\lceil p'+2^8\epsilon^{-2}\log(64/\epsilon)\rceil$. By Corollary~\ref{sift_cor}, there are $A_1,A_2$, both of density $\geq \alpha^{2q}$ such that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle \geq 1-\epsilon/32\] where \[S=\{x : \mu_A\circ \mu_A(x)\geq (1-\epsilon/16)\| \mu_A\circ \mu_A\|_{q(\mu)}\}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Sifting corollary gives dense $A_1,A_2$ concentrated on $S$.

nodes.name: Norm monotonicity places $S$ inside $S'$
nodes.statement: Since \[\| \mu_A\circ \mu_A\|_{q(\mu)}\geq \| \mu_A\circ \mu_A\|_{p'(\mu)}\geq (1+\epsilon/4)/N\] we know \[S\subseteq S'=\{x : \mu_A\circ \mu_A(x)\geq (1+\epsilon/8)/N\}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Norm monotonicity places $S$ inside $S'$.

nodes.name: Finite-field almost periodicity gives the subspace $V$
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{ap_in_ff} (applied with $\epsilon$ replaced by $\epsilon/32$) there is a subspace $V$ of codimension \[\leq 2^{37}\lo(\alpha^{2q})^2\lo(\epsilon\alpha^{2q}/32)^2\epsilon^{-2}\] such that \[\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S'}\rangle \geq 1-\tfrac{1}{16}\epsilon.\]
nodes.statement_short: Finite-field almost periodicity gives the subspace $V$.

nodes.name: Simplify the codimension bound
nodes.statement: Using $\lo(xy)\leq x^{-1}\lo(y)$ we have \[\lo(\epsilon \alpha^{2q}/32)\leq 32\epsilon^{-1}\lo(\alpha^{2q}),\] and we also use $\lo(x^y)\leq y\lo(x)$ to simplify the codimension bound to \[\leq 2^{51}q^4\lo(\alpha)^4\epsilon^{-4}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Simplify the codimension bound.

nodes.name: Bound $q$ in terms of $\epsilon$ and $\mathcal{L}(\gamma)$
nodes.statement: We further note that (using $\log x\leq x$ say) \[q\leq 2^{10}p'\epsilon^{-2}\log(64/\epsilon)\leq 2^{30}\epsilon^{-5}\lo(\gamma).\] Therefore the desired codimension bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $q$ in terms of $\epsilon$ and $\mathcal{L}(\gamma)$.

nodes.name: Chain of inequalities gives the density increment
nodes.statement:
Finally, by definition of $S'$, it follows that  egin{align*} (1+\epsilon/32)/N &\leq ((1+\epsilon/8)/N)(1-\epsilon/16)\ &\leq \langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\mu_A\circ \mu_Aangle\ &\leq 
orm{\mu_V\ast \mu_A}_\infty 
orm{\mu_{A}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \mu_{A_1}}_1\ &= 
orm{\mu_V\ast \ind{A}}_\infty\abs{A}^{-1}, \end{align*} and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Chain of inequalities gives the density increment.

nodes.name: Take a maximal chain of subspaces with density increments
nodes.statement: Let $t\geq 0$ be maximal such that there is a sequence of subspaces $\bbf_q^n=V_0\geq \cdots \geq V_t$ and associated $A_i\subseteq V_i$ with $A_0=A$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item for $0\leq i\leq t$ there exists $x_i$ such that $A_i\subseteq A-x_i$, \item with $\alpha_i=\abs{A_i}/\abs{V_i}$ we have \[\alpha_{i+1}\geq \frac{65}{64}\alpha_i\] for $0\leq i<t$, and \item \[\mathrm{codim} (V_{i+1}) \leq \mathrm{codim}(V_i)+O(\lo(\alpha)^8)\] for $0\leq i<t$. (here the second summand should be replaced with whatever explicit codimension bound we get from the above). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal chain of subspaces with density increments.

nodes.name: Set up the maximal sequence of subspaces and subsets
nodes.statement: Let $t\geq 0$ be maximal such that there is a sequence of subspaces $\bbf_q^n=V_0\geq \cdots \geq V_t$ and associated $A_i\subseteq V_i$ with $A_0=A$ such that \begin{enumerate}

nodes.statement_short: Each $A_i$ lies in a translate of $A$.

nodes.name: Densities increase by a factor $65/64$
nodes.statement: with $\alpha_i=\abs{A_i}/\abs{V_i}$ we have \[\alpha_{i+1}\geq \frac{65}{64}\alpha_i\] for $0\leq i<t$, and
nodes.statement_short: Densities increase by a factor $65/64$.

nodes.name: Codimension grows by $O(\mathcal{L}(\alpha)^8)$ per step
nodes.statement: \[\mathrm{codim} (V_{i+1}) \leq \mathrm{codim}(V_i)+O(\lo(\alpha)^8)\] for $0\leq i<t$. (here the second summand should be replaced with whatever explicit codimension bound we get from the above). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Codimension grows by $O(\mathcal{L}(\alpha)^8)$ per step.

nodes.name: The iteration has $O(\mathcal{L}(\alpha))$ steps, bounding the codimension
nodes.statement: Note this is well-defined since $t=0$ meets the requirements, and this process is finite and $t \ll \lo(\alpha)$, since $\alpha_i\leq 1$ for all $i$. Therefore \[\mathrm{codim}(V_t) \ll \lo(\alpha)^9.\]
nodes.statement_short: The iteration has $O(\mathcal{L}(\alpha))$ steps, bounding the codimension.

nodes.name: If the count is small, the finite-field density increment contradicts maximality
nodes.statement: Suppose first that \[\lvert V_t\rvert\langle \mu_{A_t}\ast \mu_{A_t},\mu_{2\cdot A_t}\rangle<1/2.\] In this case we now apply Proposition~\ref{di_in_ff} to $A_t\subseteq V_t$ with $\epsilon=1/2$ (note that $N=\lvert V_t\rvert$ and all inner product, $\mu$ etc, are relative to the ambient group $V_t$ now). Therefore there is a subspace $V\leq V_t$ of codimension (relative to $V_t$) $\ll \lo(\alpha)^8$ such that there exists some $x\in V_t$ with \[\frac{\lvert (A_t-x)\cap V\rvert}{\lvert V\rvert}=1_{A_t}\ast \mu_V(x)=\| 1_{A_t}\ast \mu_V\|_\infty \geq (1+1/64)\alpha_t,\] which contradicts the maximality of $t$, letting $V_{t+1}=V$ and $A_{t+1}=(A_t-x)\cap V_t$.
nodes.statement_short: If the count is small, the finite-field density increment contradicts maximality.

nodes.name: Hence the normalised count on $V_t$ is at least $1/2$
nodes.statement: Therefore \[\lvert V_t\rvert\langle \mu_{A_t}\ast \mu_{A_t},\mu_{2\cdot A_t}\rangle\geq 1/2.\]
nodes.statement_short: Hence the normalised count on $V_t$ is at least $1/2$.

nodes.name: 3AP-freeness evaluates the count, bounding $\alpha^2$ by $2/|V_t|$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{no3aps_inner_prod} the left-hand side is equal to $\lvert V_t\rvert/\lvert A_t\rvert^2$, and therefore \[\alpha^2 \leq \alpha_t^2 \leq 2/\lvert V_t\rvert.\]
nodes.statement_short: 3AP-freeness evaluates the count, bounding $\alpha^2$ by $2/|V_t|$.

nodes.name: Insert the codimension bound to get $n\ll\mathcal{L}(\alpha)^9$
nodes.statement: By the codimension bound the right-hand side is at most \[2q^{O(\lo(\alpha)^9)-n}.\] If $\alpha^2 \leq 2q^{-n/2}$ we are done, otherwise we deduce that $\lo(\alpha)^9 \gg n$ as required.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the codimension bound to get $n\ll\mathcal{L}(\alpha)^9$.
